title.en: Volume 378 Biographies 165: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, Zhu Qi
title.raw: 卷378 列傳一百六十五 黄爵滋 金应麟 陈庆镛 苏廷魁 朱琦

sentences.zh: 列傳一百六十五

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 165
translations.idiomatic: Biography 165

sentences.zh: 黃爵滋金應麟陳慶鏞蘇廷魁朱琦

translations.literal: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi
translations.idiomatic: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi

sentences.zh: 黃爵滋，字樹齋，江西宜黃人。

translations.literal: Huang Juezi, styled Shuzhai, was a native of Yihuang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Juezi, whose courtesy name was Shuzhai, came from Yihuang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed revising editor, and was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the third year of the Daoguang reign, entered the Hanlin as a probationary compiler, served as revising editor, and rose to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以直諫負時望，遇事鋒發，無所迴避，言屢被採納。

translations.literal: He bore the esteem of the age for his direct remonstrance; when matters arose he struck out sharply and never shrank back, and his words were repeatedly adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He won contemporary renown for forthright remonstrance, met every issue head-on without shrinking, and many of his proposals were taken up by the throne.

sentences.zh: 十五年，特擢鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was specially promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the reign he was specially promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 詔以爵滋及科道中馮贊勳、金應麟、曾望顏諸人均敢言，故特加擢任，風勵言官，開忠諫之路，勉其勿因驟得升階，即圖保位，並以誥誡臣工焉。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because Juezi and among the supervising secretaries and censors Feng Zanxun, Jin Yinglin, Zeng Wangyan, and others all dared to speak out, they were therefore specially promoted and advanced, to encourage the remonstrating officials, open the path of loyal remonstrance, exhort them not because of sudden promotion to seek only to preserve their posts, and also thereby admonish the officials as a body.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict explained that Juezi, together with the censors Feng Zanxun, Jin Yinglin, Zeng Wangyan, and others, had all spoken boldly; they were therefore given extraordinary promotions to encourage remonstrating officials, open the path of loyal counsel, and warn them not to settle into their new ranks merely to protect their positions—while offering the same admonition to the bureaucracy at large.

sentences.zh: 尋疏陳察天道，廣言路，儲將才，制匪民，整飭京城營衛，申嚴外夷防禁六事，又陳漕、河積弊，均下議行。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized on six matters: observing Heaven's way, broadening the avenue of remonstrance, storing up military talent, controlling banditry among the people, rectifying the capital garrison, and tightening prohibitions against foreigners; he also set forth accumulated abuses in the grain transport and river works, and all were sent down for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted memorials on six topics—reading the signs of Heaven, widening channels of remonstrance, cultivating military talent, curbing banditry, tightening the capital garrisons, and enforcing coastal defenses against foreigners—along with long-standing abuses in grain transport and river control; each proposal was referred for discussion and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利船艦屢至閩、浙、江南、山東洋面遊奕，測繪山川地圖。

translations.literal: At the time English ships repeatedly came to the sea off Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong on patrol, surveying and mapping mountains, rivers, and terrain.
translations.idiomatic: English vessels were then repeatedly cruising the waters off Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong, surveying coastlines and drafting maps.

sentences.zh: 爵滋疏言：「外國不可盡以恩撫，而沿海無備可危。

translations.literal: Juezi memorialized, saying: "Foreign states cannot all be treated solely with gracious appeasement, and the coast is unprepared and in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Juezi memorialized: "Foreign powers cannot all be managed by conciliation alone; our coast is undefended and exposed to grave danger."

sentences.zh: 」十八年，上禁煙議疏曰：「竊見近年銀價遞增，每銀一兩，易制錢一千六百有零，非耗銀於內地，實漏銀於外洋也。

translations.literal: " In the eighteenth year he submitted a memorial on prohibiting opium, saying: "Your servant has observed that in recent years the price of silver has risen steadily; for each tael of silver one exchanges more than sixteen hundred cash in standard coin. This is not silver being consumed within the interior, but silver actually leaking to the outer seas."
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighteenth year he submitted his famous memorial advocating an opium ban: "I have observed that silver has grown steadily dearer in recent years—each tael now exchanges for more than sixteen hundred cash. This is not domestic consumption of silver, but silver draining overseas."

sentences.zh: 蓋自鴉片流入中國，道光三年以前，每歲漏銀數百萬兩，其初不過紈褲子弟習為浮靡。

translations.literal: For since opium flowed into China, before the third year of Daoguang several million taels leaked out each year; at first it was only the sons of silk-trousered families practicing extravagant dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Since opium entered China, several million taels had been lost abroad each year even before the third year of Daoguang—at first only among pampered sons of the elite, who took it up as fashionable excess.

sentences.zh: 嗣後上自官府搢紳，下至工商優隸，以及婦女僧道，隨在吸食。

translations.literal: Afterward, from officials and gentry in government down to artisans, merchants, actors, and bond servants, as well as women, monks, and Taoist priests, smoking spread wherever one went.
translations.idiomatic: Later it spread from officials and gentry down to artisans, merchants, actors, and servants, and even to women, monks, and priests—smoking could be found everywhere.

sentences.zh: 粵省奸商勾通兵弁，用扒龍、快蟹等船，運銀出洋，運煙入口。

translations.literal: Wicked merchants in Guangdong colluded with soldiers and petty officers, using vessels such as the "dragon claw" and "fast crab" to transport silver overseas and bring opium into port.
translations.idiomatic: Rogue Guangdong merchants colluded with garrison troops, using fast smuggling craft such as the "dragon claw" and "fast crab" to ship silver abroad and opium ashore.

sentences.zh: 故自道光三年至十一年，歲漏銀一千七八百萬兩；

translations.literal: Therefore from the third year of Daoguang to the eleventh, seventeen or eighteen million taels leaked out each year;
translations.idiomatic: From the third to the eleventh year of Daoguang, the annual drain ran to seventeen or eighteen million taels;

sentences.zh: 十一年至十四年，歲漏銀二千餘萬兩；

translations.literal: from the eleventh to the fourteenth, more than twenty million taels leaked out each year;
translations.idiomatic: from the eleventh to the fourteenth year, more than twenty million taels a year;

sentences.zh: 十四年至今，漸漏至三千萬之多；

translations.literal: from the fourteenth year to the present the leak has gradually reached thirty million;
translations.idiomatic: and since the fourteenth year the loss has climbed toward thirty million;

sentences.zh: 福建、浙江、山東、天津各海口合之亦數千萬兩。

translations.literal: and the various ports of Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Tianjin together amount to tens of millions of taels as well.
translations.idiomatic: while the ports of Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Tianjin together account for tens of millions more.

sentences.zh: 以中土有用之財，填海外無窮之壑，易此害人之物，漸成病國之憂，年復一年，不知伊於胡底。

translations.literal: Using the empire's useful wealth to fill an endless gulf overseas, exchanging it for this thing that harms men, it has gradually become a worry that sickens the state; year after year, one does not know where it will end.
translations.idiomatic: We are pouring the empire's productive wealth into a bottomless foreign pit, trading it for a substance that poisons our people—a slow sickness of the state, with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 各省州縣地丁錢糧，徵錢為多，及辦奏銷，以錢為銀，前此多有贏餘，今則無不賠貼。

translations.literal: In every province, prefecture, and county the land-and-poll tax grain payments are mostly collected in cash; when accounts are rendered for imperial approval, cash is converted to silver. Formerly there was often a surplus; now there is never failure to make up a shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Land-tax collections in the provinces are mostly taken in copper cash, yet accounts to the throne must be settled in silver; where officials once reported surpluses, they now invariably make up deficits out of pocket.

sentences.zh: 各省鹽商賣鹽得錢，交課用銀，昔之爭為利藪者，今則視為畏途。

translations.literal: Salt merchants in every province sell salt for cash and pay their levies in silver; what was once fiercely contested as a source of profit is now regarded as a path of dread.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial salt merchants take payment in cash but must remit duties in silver; a trade once fought over as a gold mine is now seen as a ruinous burden.

sentences.zh: 若再數年，銀價愈貴，奏銷如何能辦？

translations.literal: If after several more years silver grows still dearer, how can the rendering of accounts be managed?
translations.idiomatic: If silver keeps rising for a few more years, how will local governments ever close their accounts?

sentences.zh: 積課如何能清？

translations.literal: How can accumulated arrears be cleared?
translations.idiomatic: How can years of tax arrears ever be cleared?

sentences.zh: 設有不測之用，又如何能支？

translations.literal: If there should be unforeseen expenditures, how could they be met?
translations.idiomatic: And if an emergency should arise, how could the treasury bear it?

sentences.zh: 今天下皆知漏卮在鴉片，而未知所以禁也。

translations.literal: Today all under Heaven know the leaking vessel is opium, yet they do not know how to prohibit it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone now knows opium is the leak in our treasury, yet no one knows how to stop it.

sentences.zh: 夫耗銀之多，由於販煙之盛；

translations.literal: The great drain of silver comes from the flourishing of opium trafficking;
translations.idiomatic: The drain of silver stems from rampant trafficking;

sentences.zh: 販煙之盛，由於食煙之眾。

translations.literal: the flourishing of trafficking comes from the multitude of smokers.
translations.idiomatic: and trafficking flourishes because smokers are so numerous.

sentences.zh: 無吸食自無興販，無興販則外洋之煙自不來矣。

translations.literal: Without smoking there is naturally no rise of trafficking; without trafficking the foreign opium will naturally not come.
translations.idiomatic: Without users there will be no trade; without trade, foreign opium will not reach our shores.

sentences.zh: 宜先重治吸食，臣請皇上准給一年期限戒菸，雖至深之癮，未有不能斷絕者。

translations.literal: One should first punish smoking heavily. Your servant asks Your Majesty to grant a one-year period to quit smoking; even the deepest addiction has none who cannot break it off.
translations.idiomatic: We should strike first at consumption. I beg Your Majesty to grant a one-year grace period for quitting; even the deepest addiction can be broken.

sentences.zh: 至一年仍然服食，是不奉法之亂民，加之重刑不足卹。

translations.literal: If after a year they still smoke, they are lawless rioters who do not obey the statutes; to impose heavy punishment on them is not excessive mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who still smoke after a year are lawless subjects; severe punishment would be no more than they deserve.

sentences.zh: 舊例吸煙罪止枷杖，其不指出興販者，罪止杖一百、徒三年，俱系活罪。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations the crime of smoking opium was only cangue and beating; those who did not denounce traffickers were punished only with one hundred blows and three years' penal servitude—all penalties short of death.
translations.idiomatic: Under existing law, smoking drew only the cangue and beating; failure to denounce traffickers meant a hundred blows and three years' exile—all punishments short of death.

sentences.zh: 斷癮之苦，甚於枷杖與徒，故不肯斷絕。

translations.literal: The suffering of breaking the addiction is worse than the cangue, beating, and exile, so they are unwilling to break it off.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal hurts more than the cangue or exile, so addicts refuse to quit.

sentences.zh: 若罪以死論，臨刑之慘急，苦於斷癮之苟延，臣知其原死於家而不原死於市。

translations.literal: If the crime were judged by death, the agony and urgency at the moment of execution would be more bitter than the lingering pain of breaking the addiction; your servant knows they would rather die at home than die in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Make smoking a capital crime, and the terror of the execution ground would outweigh the misery of withdrawal; I am confident most would rather die at home than on the scaffold.

sentences.zh: 況我皇上​​雷霆之威，赫然震怒，雖愚頑沉溺之久，自足以發聾振瞶。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Our Emperor's thunderbolt majesty is manifest in sudden wrath, even those long stupid, stubborn, and sunk in addiction will of themselves be enough to have their deafness opened and their blindness shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Your Majesty's thunderous wrath is made plain, even the most stubborn long-term addict will be shaken awake.

sentences.zh: 皇上之旨嚴，則奉法之吏肅，犯法之人畏。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's orders are strict, the law-abiding officials are solemn, and those who violate the law are in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Strict imperial orders make officials enforce the law and make offenders afraid.

sentences.zh: 一年之內，尚未用刑，十已戒其八九。

translations.literal: Within one year, before punishments have even been applied, eight or nine out of ten will already have quit.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, even before executions begin, eight or nine in ten will have quit on their own.

sentences.zh: 已食者藉國法以保餘生，未食者因炯戒以全身命，止闢之大權，即好生之盛德也。

translations.literal: Those who have smoked will rely on the nation's law to preserve the remainder of their lives; those who have not smoked will, through bright warning, preserve their persons whole. To exercise the great power of prohibition is itself the supreme virtue of cherishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Former smokers will be saved by the law; the never-addicted will be warned off in time. To ban opium decisively is itself an act of mercy.

sentences.zh: 伏請飭諭各督撫嚴行清查保甲，初先曉諭，定於一年後取具五家互結，準令舉發，給予優獎。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully asks that orders be sent to every governor-general and governor to carry out strict investigation through the baojia system, first instructing the people, fixing that after one year five-house mutual guarantees be obtained, allowing denunciations, and granting generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to order every governor to enforce the baojia household registers: first educate the people, then after one year require five-house mutual guarantees, allow informers, and reward them generously.

sentences.zh: 倘有容隱，本犯照新例處死，互結之家照例治罪。

translations.literal: If there is concealment, the principal offender shall be executed according to the new regulations, and the mutually guaranteeing households punished according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who conceals an offender will see the smoker executed under the new law and the guaranteeing neighbors punished as well.

sentences.zh: 通都大邑，往來客商，責成店鋪，如有容留食煙之人，照窩藏匪類治罪。

translations.literal: In great cities and metropolitan districts, for traveling merchants and guests, shops shall be held responsible; if they harbor smokers, they shall be punished as for concealing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In major cities, innkeepers who lodge traveling merchants must answer for their guests; harboring smokers will be treated like harboring bandits.

sentences.zh: 文武大小各官，照常人加等，子孫不准考試。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of every rank shall have their penalties increased one degree above ordinary persons, and their descendants shall not be permitted to sit for examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of every rank shall face penalties one degree harsher than commoners, and their descendants shall be barred from the examinations.

sentences.zh: 官親幕友家丁，除本犯治罪外，本管官嚴加議處。

translations.literal: For officials' kin, secretaries, staff, and household retainers, besides punishing the principal offender, the supervising official shall be severely dealt with by deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives, secretaries, or servants of officials are involved, the offenders will be punished and their supervising official severely disciplined.

sentences.zh: 滿、漢官兵，照地方官保甲辦理；

translations.literal: Manchu and Han officers and soldiers shall be handled according to the baojia procedures of local officials;
translations.idiomatic: Manchu and Han troops shall be registered and inspected under the same baojia rules as civilians;

sentences.zh: 管轄失察之人，照地方官辦理。

translations.literal: those in jurisdiction who fail in supervision shall be handled as local officials are handled.
translations.idiomatic: and commanders who fail to detect offenders shall be punished like negligent local officials.

sentences.zh: 庶幾軍民一體，上下肅清，漏卮可塞，銀價不至再昂，然後講求理財之方，誠天下萬世臣民之福也。

translations.literal: Thus perhaps army and people will be one body, high and low purified, the leaking vessel can be stopped, and the price of silver will not rise again; only then can methods of managing state finances be pursued—truly the blessing of all under Heaven for ten thousand generations of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Then soldiers and civilians alike may be cleansed, the drain stopped, and silver stabilized—so that sound fiscal policy becomes possible again. That would be a blessing for the empire and its people for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，上深韙之，下疆臣各抒所見，速議章程。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, the Emperor deeply approved it and sent it down to frontier officials to each set forth their views and quickly deliberate regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted; the Emperor strongly approved it and ordered provincial officials to submit opinions and draft regulations at once.

sentences.zh: 先是，太常寺少卿許乃濟疏言，煙禁雖嚴，閉關不可，徒法不行，請仍用舊制納稅，以貨易貨，不得用銀購買，吸食罪名，專重官員、士子、兵丁，時皆謂非政體。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xu Naiji had memorialized that although the opium ban was strict, closing the ports was impossible and empty law would not be enforced; he asked to restore the old system of paying tax, trading goods for goods, not permitting purchase with silver, and laying the heaviest penalties for smoking on officials, scholars, and soldiers—at the time all said this was not proper statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Naiji of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had argued that strict prohibition was futile while the ports stayed closed, and proposed legalizing opium under tax, bartering goods instead of silver, and reserving harsh penalties for officials, scholars, and soldiers—an approach widely condemned as unsound policy.

sentences.zh: 爵滋劾乃濟，罷其職，連擢爵滋大理寺少卿、通政使、禮部侍郎，調刑部。

translations.literal: Juezi impeached Naiji and he was dismissed from office; Juezi was in succession promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, commissioner of the Office of Transmission, vice minister of Rites, and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi impeached Xu Naiji, who was dismissed; Juezi was then promoted in rapid succession to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, transmission commissioner, vice minister of Rites, and finally transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十九年，廷臣議定販煙、吸煙罪名新例，略如爵滋所請。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the court ministers deliberated and fixed new regulations for the crimes of trafficking and smoking opium, broadly as Juezi had requested.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the court enacted new penalties for trafficking and smoking opium, largely along the lines Juezi had proposed.

sentences.zh: 林則徐至粵，盡焚躉船存煙，議外國人販煙罪。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong, burned all the opium stored on the receiving ships, and deliberated the crime of foreigners trafficking opium.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Zexu reached Guangdong he burned all the opium held on foreign receiving ships and pressed charges against foreign traffickers.

sentences.zh: 英領事義律不就約束，兵釁遂開。

translations.literal: The English consul Charles Elliot would not submit to restraint, and military hostilities thereupon opened.
translations.idiomatic: The British consul Charles Elliot refused to comply, and war broke out.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命爵滋偕左都御史祁俊藻赴福建查辦禁煙，與總督鄧廷楨籌備海防。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Juezi was ordered, together with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao, to go to Fujian to investigate and handle the opium prohibition, and with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen to plan coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Juezi was sent to Fujian with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao to oversee the opium ban and, with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen, to prepare coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 洎英兵來犯，廷楨屢挫敵於廈門，上疑之。

translations.literal: When English troops came to attack, Tingzhen repeatedly defeated the enemy at Xiamen; the Emperor was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces attacked, Deng Tingzhen reported repeated victories at Xiamen, but the throne grew skeptical.

sentences.zh: 爵滋與俊藻方至浙江按事，復命赴福建察奏。

translations.literal: Juezi and Junzao had just reached Zhejiang on an investigative mission when they were again ordered to go to Fujian to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi and Qi Junzao had just reached Zhejiang on another assignment when they were ordered back to Fujian to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「廷楨所奏不誣；

translations.literal: They memorialized, stating: "Tingzhen's reports are not false;
translations.idiomatic: They reported: "Deng Tingzhen's accounts are not false;

sentences.zh: 定海不可不速復；

translations.literal: Dinghai cannot but be swiftly recovered;
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai must be retaken without delay;

sentences.zh: 水師有專門之技，宜破格用人。

translations.literal: the navy has specialized skills and one should employ men by breaking through regular rules."
translations.idiomatic: the navy requires specialized skill and men should be appointed outside normal seniority rules."

sentences.zh: 」具言戰守方略。

translations.literal: " They set forth in detail strategies for fighting and defense.
translations.idiomatic: " They laid out detailed plans for offense and defense.

sentences.zh: 又言浙江為閩、粵之心腹，與江蘇為脣齒，請飭伊里布不可偏聽琦善，信敵必退。

translations.literal: They also said that Zhejiang is the heart and belly of Fujian and Guangdong, and with Jiangsu is lip and teeth; they asked that Yilibu be instructed not to listen one-sidedly to Qishan and believe the enemy would certainly withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: They also warned that Zhejiang was the strategic heart of Fujian and Guangdong and the close partner of Jiangsu, and urged that Yilibu not heed Qishan alone or assume the enemy would simply withdraw.

sentences.zh: 及回京，復極言英人勞師襲遠不足慮，宜竟與絕市，募兵節餉，為持久計，以海防圖進。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital they again spoke urgently that the English, wearied in campaigning and striking from afar, were not worth worrying over; one should simply cut off trade with them entirely, raise troops and economize on pay, make long-term plans, and present a coastal defense map.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing they argued that Britain, fighting far from home with overextended forces, was not to be feared; the court should cut off trade entirely, raise troops, tighten spending, plan for a long war, and they submitted a coastal defense map.

sentences.zh: 既而琦善在粵議撫不得要領，連歲命將出師，廣東、浙江皆不利。

translations.literal: Before long Qishan in Guangdong negotiated appeasement without grasping essentials; year after year generals were ordered to take the field, and in both Guangdong and Zhejiang affairs went badly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qishan bungled peace talks in Guangdong; generals were sent out year after year, and campaigns in Guangdong and Zhejiang both went badly.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，英兵由海入江，乃定和議於江寧，煙禁自此弛矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year English troops entered the Yangzi from the sea, and peace was settled at Jiangning; from this the opium prohibition was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year British forces advanced up the Yangzi from the sea; peace was signed at Nanjing, and the opium ban was effectively abandoned.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂去官。

translations.literal: Soon after he left office on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 爵滋為御史時，稽察戶部銀庫，嘗疏言庫丁輕收虧帑之弊。

translations.literal: When Juezi was a censor he inspected the Ministry of Revenue silver vault and once memorialized on the abuse of vault clerks taking light receipts and causing treasury deficits.
translations.idiomatic: As a censor Juezi had inspected the Ministry of Revenue silver vault and warned that clerks were accepting short payments and draining the treasury.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，銀庫虧空九百萬兩事發，追論管庫、查庫諸臣，罪皆褫職責賠，賠既足，次第予官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the matter of a nine-million-tael deficit in the silver vault came to light; those who had managed and inspected the vault were pursued for judgment, all were stripped of office and ordered to compensate; once compensation was complete they were in turn given office again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year a nine-million-tael vault shortfall was exposed; vault managers and inspectors were dismissed and ordered to repay; once repayment was complete they were gradually restored to office.

sentences.zh: 爵滋以員外郎候補，病足家居，上猶時問其何在。

translations.literal: Juezi awaited appointment as an outside-section director; ill in the feet he remained at home, yet the Emperor still from time to time asked where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi awaited appointment as a department director but stayed home with a foot ailment; the Emperor still occasionally inquired after him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，至京，會上崩，遂不出。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he reached the capital; it happened that the Emperor died, and he therefore did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he came to Beijing, but the Emperor died before he could take office, and he never served again.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，卒。

translations.literal: After more than three years he died.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 爵滋以詩名，喜交遊，每夜閉閣草奏，日騎出，遍視諸故人名士，飲酒賦詩，意氣豪甚。

translations.literal: Juezi was famed for poetry and loved making friends; each night he closed his study to draft memorials, by day rode out and visited all his old friends and famous men, drinking wine and composing poetry, his spirit very bold.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi was known as a poet and a convivial man: he drafted memorials at night, rode out by day to visit friends and luminaries, drinking and composing verse with exuberant spirit.

sentences.zh: 及創議禁煙，始終主戰，一時以為清流眉目。

translations.literal: When he initiated the proposal to prohibit opium he always advocated war; for a time he was regarded as the leading figure of the moralist faction.
translations.idiomatic: When he launched the drive to ban opium he consistently favored war, and for a time was seen as the leading voice of the moralist "pure stream" faction.

sentences.zh: 所著奏議、詩文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected memorials and poetry circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and collected poems circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 金應麟，字亞伯，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Jin Yinglin, styled Yabo, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yinglin, whose courtesy name was Yabo, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為中書。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased entry as a secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，成進士，授刑部主事，總辦秋審，先後從大臣讞獄四川、湖北、山西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, took charge of the autumn assizes, and successively followed high ministers in reviewing cases in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Daoguang, joined the Ministry of Punishments as a principal clerk, oversaw the autumn judicial review, and accompanied senior officials on capital-case reviews in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 累擢郎中，改御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, changed to censor, and transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to department director, became a censor, and was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏請修改刑例，於鬥毆、報盜、劫囚、誣告、私鑄、服舍違式、斷罪引律、奴婢毆主、故禁故勘平人、應捕人追捕罪人、犯罪存留養親、官司出入人罪、徒流遷徙地方、外省駐防逃人，逐條論列，多被採取改定；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting revision of the penal code, setting forth article by article on brawling, reporting bandits, rescuing prisoners, false accusation, private coining, violation of mourning and residence regulations, citing statutes in judgment, slaves and maids beating masters, wrongful imprisonment and torture of commoners, authorized pursuers chasing criminals, crimes with retention for supporting parents, officials improperly releasing or entering persons into guilt, places of exile and penal servitude, and fugitives from garrisons in outer provinces—many were adopted and revised;
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for revisions to the penal code, addressing brawling, bandit reports, prison breaks, false accusations, private coining, mourning violations, statutory citations, assaults on masters by bondservants, wrongful imprisonment, pursuit of fugitives, filial-retention cases, official malfeasance in sentencing, exile destinations, and garrison deserters—many of his proposals were adopted;

sentences.zh: 又論銅船恣橫不法及驛站擾累諸弊，並下各省督撫禁革。

translations.literal: he also discussed abuses such as copper-transport boats acting lawlessly and postal stations harassing and burdening the people, and orders were sent down to every provincial governor-general and governor to prohibit and abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: he also exposed abuses by copper-transport fleets and postal stations; orders went out to every province to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 先後封事數十上，劾疆臣琦善、河臣吳邦慶尤為時稱。

translations.literal: In succession he submitted several tens of sealed memorials; his impeachments of frontier minister Qishan and river commissioner Wu Bangqing were especially praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted dozens of sealed memorials; his attacks on Qishan and river commissioner Wu Bangqing won particular acclaim.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉其敢言，擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor commended his bold speech and promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor praised his outspokenness and promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遭憂歸，服闋，授鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: He returned home on bereavement; when mourning ended he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for a parent he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 疏論水師廢弛，漕政頹紊。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the navy's decay and neglect and the grain transport administration's decline and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the decay of the navy and the disorder of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出為直隸按察使，鞫護理長蘆鹽運使楊成業等得贓獄，論遣戍，前運使陳崇禮等並罣議。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried acting Changlu salt transport commissioner Yang Chengye and others in a bribery case, judged them for banishment to frontier service, and former transport commissioner Chen Chongli and others were also implicated in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried acting Changlu salt commissioner Yang Chengye and others for bribery, sentenced them to exile, and implicated former commissioner Chen Chongli and others.

sentences.zh: 尋召為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「海疆諸臣欺罔，其故由於爵祿之念重，而趨避之計工。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized, saying: "The coastal officials deceive and mislead; the reason is that thoughts of rank and salary weigh heavily, while schemes of evasion and avoidance are finely wrought."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he wrote: "Coastal officials deceive the throne because they prize rank and salary and excel at evading responsibility."

sentences.zh: 欲破其欺，是在乾斷。

translations.literal: To break their deception lies in resolute decision.
translations.idiomatic: To break their deception requires decisive imperial action.

sentences.zh: 資格不可拘，嫌疑不必避，舊過不妨宥，重賞不宜惜。

translations.literal: Seniority qualifications must not be rigidly bound; suspicion need not be avoided; old faults may be pardoned; heavy rewards should not be stinted.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be bound by seniority, avoid no one for suspicion, pardon past faults, and spare no reward.

sentences.zh: 近頃長江海口鎮兵足守，而敵船深入，逃潰時聞。

translations.literal: Recently at the Yangzi estuary garrison troops were sufficient to defend, yet enemy ships penetrated deep, and flight and rout were heard from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Recently at the Yangzi estuary there were troops enough to hold the line, yet enemy ships penetrated deep inland and rout was reported again and again.

sentences.zh: 竭億萬氓庶之脂膏。

translations.literal: They exhaust the fat and cream of hundreds of millions of common people.
translations.idiomatic: They drain the substance of millions of common people

sentences.zh: 保一二庸臣之軀命。

translations.literal: to preserve the persons and lives of one or two mediocre officials.
translations.idiomatic: to preserve the lives of a few mediocre officials.

sentences.zh: 議者諉謂無人無兵無餉無械。

translations.literal: Those who discuss the matter shift blame, saying there are no men, no troops, no pay, no weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors excuse failure by claiming there are no men, no troops, no funds, and no arms.

sentences.zh: 竊以無人當求，無兵當練，無餉械亦當計度固有，多則持重，少則用謀，作三軍之氣，定邊疆之危，在皇上假以事權，與任事者運用一心而已。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if there are no men one should seek them, if there are no troops one should train them; if there are no pay and weapons one should also plan what is already on hand—if many, hold firm; if few, use stratagem; rouse the spirit of the three armies and settle the peril of the frontier—it lies only in the Emperor's granting discretionary authority and the responsible officials' working in one mind.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that men must be found, troops must be trained, and existing funds and arms must be used wisely—mass when strong, maneuver when weak, rouse the army's spirit, and secure the frontier. All that is needed is that Your Majesty delegate authority and that those in charge act as one.

sentences.zh: 」复疏進預計度支圖、火器圖、籌海戰方略甚悉。

translations.literal: " He again memorialized and presented charts of projected revenue and expenditure, charts of firearms, and coastal war plans in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: " He also submitted detailed charts of projected revenue, firearms, and coastal war plans.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以親老乞歸省，不復出。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because his parents were aged he begged to return home to attend them and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he asked leave to care for aged parents and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 著有廌華堂奏議及駢體文。

translations.literal: He authored the memorials of the Lihua Hall and parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: He left memorials collected as the Lihua Hall Papers and works in parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 陳慶鏞，字頌南，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Chen Qingyong, styled Songnan, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingyong, whose courtesy name was Songnan, came from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授戶部主事，遷員外郎，授御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, on leaving the academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to outside-section director, and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the twelfth year of Daoguang, served in the Hanlin, then joined the Ministry of Revenue as a principal clerk, rose to department director, and became a censor.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，海疆僨事，獲罪諸臣浸復起用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, with the coastal crisis, officials who had been punished were gradually reemployed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, as the coastal war wound down, disgraced officials were gradually brought back into service.

sentences.zh: 慶鏞上疏論刑賞失措，曰：「行政之要，莫大於刑賞。

translations.literal: Qingyong submitted a memorial on the mishandling of punishments and rewards, saying: "In administering affairs nothing is greater than punishments and rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingyong memorialized on the mishandling of punishments and rewards: "In government nothing matters more than how punishments and rewards are applied."

sentences.zh: 刑賞之權，操之於君，喻之於民，所以示天下之大公也。

translations.literal: The power of punishments and rewards is wielded by the ruler and made known to the people—thereby the great impartiality of all under Heaven is displayed.
translations.idiomatic: That power rests with the ruler and must be made clear to the people, for it embodies the empire's impartial justice.

sentences.zh: 大學論平天下之道，在於絜矩。

translations.literal: The Great Learning discusses the way to pacify all under Heaven as lying in the measuring square.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Learning teaches that bringing peace to the realm depends on holding the measuring square—applying the same standard to oneself that one applies to others.

sentences.zh: 矩者何，民之好惡是已。

translations.literal: What is the square? It is the people's likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: What is the measuring square? The people's likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 海疆多事以來，自總督、將軍以至州縣丞倅，禽駭獸奔。

translations.literal: Since the coastal troubles began, from governors-general and generals down to prefectural, county, assistant, and vice officials, they were like birds in fright and beasts in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Since the coastal war began, governors-general and generals down to county deputies scattered in panic like frightened birds and fleeing beasts.

sentences.zh: 皇上赫然震怒，失律之罪，法有莫逭。

translations.literal: The Emperor was manifestly enraged; the crime of violating military discipline—under the law there is no escape.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's wrath was terrible, and under the law no one who broke military discipline could escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 於是辱國之將軍奕山、奕經，參贊文蔚，總督牛鑑，提督餘步雲，先後就逮，步雲伏法。

translations.literal: Thereupon the nation-disgracing generals Yishan and Yijing, staff officer Wenwei, Governor-General Niujian, and Commander Yu Buyun were in succession arrested; Buyun was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: The disgraced generals Yishan and Yijing, staff officer Wenwei, Governor-General Niujian, and Commander Yu Buyun were arrested one after another; Buyun was executed.

sentences.zh: 血氣之倫，罔不拊手稱快，謂國法前雖未伸於琦善，今猶伸於餘步雲。

translations.literal: Men of passionate spirit all clapped their hands in satisfaction, saying that although state law had before not been applied to Qishan, it was now applied to Yu Buyun.
translations.idiomatic: Spirited men everywhere applauded, saying that although Qishan had escaped justice before, the law had at last been applied to Yu Buyun.

sentences.zh: 乃未幾起琦善為葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: Yet before long Qishan was raised to assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet soon Qishan was restored as assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 邸報既傳，人情震駭，猶解之曰：'古聖王之待罪人，有投四裔以御魑魅者。

translations.literal: When the court gazette had spread, popular sentiment was shaken with alarm; yet some explained it, saying: "The ancient sage kings in dealing with criminals had those cast into the four borderlands to repel evil spirits."
translations.idiomatic: When the court gazette spread the news, public shock was widespread; some tried to explain it away: "Ancient sage kings sometimes banished criminals to the frontier to ward off evil spirits."

sentences.zh: '皇上之於琦善，殆其類是，而今且以三品頂戴用為熱河都統矣，且用奕經為葉爾羌幫辦大臣，文蔚為古城領隊大臣矣。

translations.literal: "The Emperor's treatment of Qishan is probably of this kind—and now he is even employed with a third-rank button as commander of Rehe, and Yijing is employed as assistant commissioner at Yarkand, and Wenwei as brigade commander at Gucheng."
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor's handling of Qishan may be of that sort—but now Qishan has been appointed commander of Rehe with a third-rank button, Yijing made assistant commissioner at Yarkand, and Wenwei brigade commander at Gucheng."

sentences.zh: 琦善於戰事方始，首先示弱，以惰軍心，海內糜爛，至於此極。

translations.literal: Qishan, when the war had just begun, was first to show weakness and thereby slacken army morale; the empire was wasted and ruined to this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: At the very start of the war Qishan was the first to show weakness and sap the army's morale; the empire was brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 既罷斥終身不齒，猶恐不足饜民心而作士氣。

translations.literal: Though dismissed and for life counted unworthy, one still fears this is not enough to satisfy the people's hearts and raise soldiers' morale.
translations.idiomatic: Even permanent dismissal and disgrace may not be enough to satisfy public anger or restore the troops' fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 奕經之罪，雖較琦善稍減，文蔚之罪，較奕經又減。

translations.literal: Yijing's guilt, though somewhat less than Qishan's; Wenwei's guilt, less than Yijing's again.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing's guilt was somewhat less than Qishan's, and Wenwei's less than Yijing's.

sentences.zh: 然皇上命將出師，若何慎重。

translations.literal: Yet when the Emperor orders generals to take the field, how careful should one be?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Emperor sends generals to war, how grave a matter that is.

sentences.zh: 奕經頓兵半載，曾未身歷行間，騁其虛憍之氣，自詭一鼓而復三城；

translations.literal: Yijing halted his army half a year, never personally passing through the ranks, displaying his empty arrogance, falsely claiming he would recover three cities in one drumbeat;
translations.idiomatic: Yijing kept his army idle for half a year, never once entering the ranks himself, swaggering with empty pride and boasting that one assault would retake three cities;

sentences.zh: 卒之機事不密，貽笑敵人，覆軍殺將，一敗不支。

translations.literal: In the end plans were not kept secret, he made the enemy laugh, the army was overturned and generals killed, and after one defeat he could not hold up.
translations.idiomatic: in the end his plans leaked, he became a laughingstock to the enemy, his army was destroyed and his generals killed, and one defeat undid him completely.

sentences.zh: 此不待別科騷擾供億、招權納賄之罪，而已不可勝誅。

translations.literal: These need not wait for separate listing of crimes of harassment, supply burdens, abuse of power, and accepting bribes—already they are beyond what can be punished in full.
translations.idiomatic: Without even counting his harassment of the people, waste of supplies, abuse of power, and bribery, his offenses were already beyond full punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣亦知奕經為高宗純皇帝之裔，皇上親親睦族，不忍遽加顯戮。

translations.literal: Your servant also knows that Yijing is a descendant of the Gaozong Chun Emperor; the Emperor treats kin with affection and reconciles the clan, and is unwilling to hastily impose conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant knows that Yijing is a descendant of the Qianlong Emperor, and that Your Majesty, cherishing kin and clan harmony, would be reluctant to execute him outright.

sentences.zh: 然即幸邀寬典，亦當禁錮終身，無為天潢宗室羞，豈圖收禁未及三月，輒复棄瑕錄用？

translations.literal: Yet even if fortunate enough to receive leniency, he should be confined for life, and not bring shame on the imperial clan—who would have thought that after detention of less than three months he would again be restored despite his flaws?
translations.idiomatic: Yet even if spared by mercy, he should be confined for life rather than bring shame on the imperial house—who imagined that after less than three months in custody he would be restored despite his faults?

sentences.zh: 且此數人者，皇上特未知其見惡於民之深耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, as for these several men, the Emperor simply does not yet know how deeply they are hated by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty may not yet realize how deeply these men are hated by the people.

sentences.zh: 倘俯採輿論，孰不切齒琦善為罪魁，誰不疾首於奕山、奕經、牛鑑、文蔚，而以為投畀之不容緩？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would bow to collect public opinion, who would not gnash teeth at Qishan as chief culprit, who would not be distraught over Yishan, Yijing, Niujian, and Wenwei, and not hold that casting them away cannot be delayed?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would heed public opinion, who would not gnash his teeth at Qishan as the chief culprit, or be anguished over Yishan, Yijing, Niujian, and Wenwei, and demand that they be cast out without delay?

sentences.zh: 此非臣一人之私言也。

translations.literal: This is not Your servant's private opinion alone.
translations.idiomatic: This is not my private opinion alone.

sentences.zh: 側聞琦善意侈體汰，跋扈如常，葉爾羌之行，本屬怏怏；

translations.literal: On the side one hears that Qishan is intentionally extravagant and dissolute in deportment, overbearing as before; the journey to Yarkand was inherently resentful;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard on the side that Qishan remains as extravagant and overbearing as ever, and resented his assignment to Yarkand;

sentences.zh: 今果未及出關，即蒙召還。

translations.literal: Now as expected, before even passing out of the frontier pass, he received recall.
translations.idiomatic: and as expected, before he had even crossed the frontier he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 熱河密邇神京，有識無識，莫不撫膺太息，以為皇上鄉用琦善之意，尚不止此。

translations.literal: Rehe is close to the sacred capital; the knowing and the unknowing alike all beat their breasts and sigh deeply, thinking the Emperor's intent to reuse Qishan locally does not stop here.
translations.idiomatic: Rehe lies close to the capital; learned and common people alike beat their breasts and sigh, fearing the Emperor's plan to reuse Qishan does not end here.

sentences.zh: 萬一有事，則熒惑聖聰者，必仍系斯人。

translations.literal: If perchance trouble arises, the one who will beguile the sacred mind must still be this man.
translations.idiomatic: If trouble should arise, the one who will mislead Your Majesty will surely be this same man.

sentences.zh: 履霜堅冰，深可懍懼。

translations.literal: Treading frost leads to solid ice—deeply to be feared with trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Tread on frost and solid ice follows—a prospect that fills one with dread.

sentences.zh: 頃者禦試翰詹，以'烹阿封即墨'命題，而今茲刑賞顧如此，臣未知皇上所謂阿者何人？

translations.literal: Recently at the imperial examination for Hanlin, the topic "Execute A and enfeoff Jimo" was set—yet now punishments and rewards look thus; Your servant does not know who the Emperor means by "A"?
translations.idiomatic: At the recent Hanlin imperial examination the topic was "Execute A and enfeoff Jimo"—yet now punishments and rewards look like this; I do not know whom Your Majesty considers "A."

sentences.zh: 即墨者何人？

translations.literal: Who is "Jimo"?
translations.idiomatic: And who is "Jimo"?

sentences.zh: 假如聖意高深，偶或差忒，而以即墨為阿，阿為即墨，將毋譽之毀之者有以淆亂是非耶？

translations.literal: If the sacred intention is profound and there should happen to be some error, and Jimo is taken for A and A for Jimo, will those who praise and those who slander not thereby have means to confuse right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's intent is too subtle and a mistake is made—if Jimo is treated as A and A as Jimo—will those who praise and those who slander not use it to confuse right and wrong?

sentences.zh: 所望皇上立奮天威，收回成命，體大學絜矩之旨，鑑盈廷毀譽之真，國法稍伸，民心可慰。

translations.literal: What is hoped is that the Emperor will immediately rouse Heaven's authority, withdraw the issued orders, embody the Great Learning's aim of the measuring square, discern the truth of praise and blame filling the court, let state law be somewhat applied, and the people's hearts be consoled.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to rouse imperial authority at once, withdraw these appointments, uphold the Great Learning's principle of the measuring square, discern the true praise and blame in the court, let the law be upheld, and console the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，宣宗嘉之，諭曰：「朕無知人之明，以致琦善、奕經、文蔚諸人喪師失律，惟有反躬自責，不欲諉罪臣工。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, the Xuanzong Emperor commended it and instructed: "We lack the discernment to know men, so that Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and others lost armies and violated discipline—we can only turn inward in self-blame and do not wish to shift guilt onto officials."
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the Xuanzong Emperor praised it and said: "I lack the discernment to choose men wisely, and so Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and others lost armies and broke discipline. I can only blame myself and do not wish to shift guilt onto my officials."

sentences.zh: 今該御史請收回成命，朕非文過飾非之君，豈肯回護？

translations.literal: Now this censor asks to withdraw the issued orders; We are not a ruler who covers faults and prettifies errors—how could We protect them?
translations.idiomatic: Now this censor asks me to withdraw those appointments. I am not a ruler who covers faults and prettifies errors—how could I protect them?

sentences.zh: 」复革琦善等職，令閉門思過。

translations.literal: " Qishan and the others were again stripped of office and ordered to reflect on their faults behind closed doors.
translations.idiomatic: " Qishan and the others were again dismissed and ordered to reflect on their faults at home.

sentences.zh: 於是直聲震海內。

translations.literal: Thereupon his reputation for direct speech shook the empire.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for outspoken integrity then resounded throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷給事中，巡視東城，以事詿吏議，左遷光祿寺署正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to supervising secretary, inspected the Eastern Ward, and because of a matter was entangled in official deliberation and demoted to acting registrar of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he became a supervising secretary and inspected the Eastern Ward; implicated in an official inquiry, he was demoted to acting registrar of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，乞歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，以大學士朱鳳標薦，复授御史，蹶而再起，氣不少撓，疊上疏多關大計。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended, on Grand Secretary Zhu Fengbiao's recommendation he was again appointed censor; though he stumbled he rose again, his spirit not much bent, and repeatedly submitted memorials mostly touching great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, Grand Secretary Zhu Fengbiao recommended him and he was restored as censor; though he had fallen, he rose again with undiminished spirit and submitted many memorials on matters of state.

sentences.zh: 自粵匪起，福建群盜蠢動，蔓延泉、漳、興、永諸郡。

translations.literal: Since the Guangdong rebels rose, bandits in Fujian stirred restlessly and spread through the prefectures of Quan, Zhang, Xing, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taiping rebellion began, bandits stirred throughout Fujian and spread through Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, Xinghua, and Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，慶鏞疏陳利害，命回籍治團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Qingyong memorialized on advantages and dangers and was ordered to return to his native place to manage militia training.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, Chen Qingyong memorialized on the crisis and was ordered home to organize local militia.

sentences.zh: 惠安妖婦邱氏煽亂，偵獲置諸法，賜花翎。

translations.literal: A sorceress surnamed Qiu in Huian stirred rebellion; she was detected, seized, and punished by law, and he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He detected and punished a sorceress surnamed Qiu who had stirred rebellion in Huian, and was rewarded with a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 俄以病請開缺。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave of office on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 七年，逆匪林俊糾莆陽、仙遊、永春、南安群賊犯泉州，慶鏞激厲士民固守，賊攻圍數日而退。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the rebel bandit Lin Jun gathered bandits from Puyang, Xianyou, Yongchun, and Nan'an to attack Quanzhou; Qingyong roused officials and people to hold firm, and after several days of siege the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the rebel Lin Jun rallied bandits from Puyang, Xianyou, Yongchun, and Nan'an to attack Quanzhou; Chen Qingyong roused officials and people to hold the city, and after several days of siege the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 論功，以道員候選。

translations.literal: On assessment of merit he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒於泉州，贈光祿寺卿，賜祭葬，廕一子知縣，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at Quanzhou; he was posthumously granted Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, given sacrificial rites and burial honors, one son was ennobled as county magistrate, and he was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at Quanzhou; he was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted state funeral honors, and one son was ennobled as county magistrate; he was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.

sentences.zh: 慶鏞精研漢學​​，而製行則服膺宋儒，文辭樸茂，著有籀經堂文集、三家詩考、說文釋、古籀考等書。

translations.literal: Qingyong deeply studied Han Learning, yet in conduct followed Song Confucians; his prose was plain and abundant; he authored works including the Choujing Hall Collected Writings, Examination of the Three Schools of Poetry, Explanation of the Shuowen, and Study of Ancient Zhou Script, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingyong was a scholar of Han Learning who in conduct followed the Song Confucians; his prose was plain and solid. He wrote the Choujing Hall Collected Writings, Examination of the Three Schools of Poetry, Explanation of the Shuowen, Study of Ancient Zhou Script, and other works.

sentences.zh: 蘇廷魁，字賡堂，廣東高要人。

translations.literal: Su Tingkui, styled Gengtang, was a native of Gaoyao in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Su Tingkui, whose courtesy name was Gengtang, came from Gaoyao in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed revising editor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin, and served as revising editor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became a censor.

sentences.zh: 海疆兵事方亟，迭上疏論列，請修築虎門砲台及燕塘墟、大沙河、龜岡諸要隘，以防敵回擾粵，既而和議成。

translations.literal: While coastal military affairs were urgent, he repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth views, requesting construction of Humen batteries and the strategic passes at Yantangxu, Dashaha, and Guigang to guard against the enemy returning to harass Guangdong; afterward peace was negotiated.
translations.idiomatic: While the coastal war was urgent he submitted repeated memorials calling for fortification of Humen batteries and the passes at Yantangxu, Dashaha, and Guigang to guard against a renewed enemy attack on Guangdong; peace was soon negotiated.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，有白氣自天西南隅直掃參旗，因災異上疏數千言，極論時政乖迕，歸罪樞臣穆彰阿等，請立罷黜；

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year a white vapor swept straight from the southwest corner of Heaven toward the Shen constellation; because of this omen he submitted a memorial of several thousand characters, urgently discussing how current policy went astray, blaming Grand Council member Mu Zhang'a and others, and requesting immediate dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year a white vapor swept from the southwest sky toward the Shen constellation; citing this omen he submitted a memorial of several thousand characters denouncing current policy, blaming Grand Council member Mu Zhang'a and others, and demanding their immediate dismissal;

sentences.zh: 並下罪己詔，開直諫之路：語多指斥。

translations.literal: And also issuing an edict of self-reproach and opening the path of direct remonstrance—the language was largely accusatory.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged an edict of self-reproach and an open path for direct remonstrance—much of his language was accusatory.

sentences.zh: 宣宗覽奏動容，嘉其切直，朝野傾望丰采。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor reading the memorial was moved, commended its blunt directness, and court and country alike looked to him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor was moved by the memorial and praised its blunt honesty; court and country alike looked to him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 遭憂去官，服闋，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He left office on bereavement; when mourning ended he was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for a parent he was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，上謹始疏，請求宏濟之道，執勞謙之義，防驕泰之萌，推誠任賢，慎始圖治，選擇翰詹為講官，嚴取孝廉方正備採用，文宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he submitted a memorial on careful beginnings, requesting the great way of aid in need, holding to the righteousness of labor and humility, guarding against the sprouting of pride and excess, extending sincerity and trusting the worthy, being careful at the start in planning good governance, selecting Hanlin for lecture posts, strictly choosing filial and incorrupt graduates for use—the Wenzong Emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he submitted a memorial on careful beginnings, urging broad policies of relief, diligence and humility, vigilance against pride, sincerity in appointing talent, careful planning at the start of rule, selection of Hanlin scholars as lecturers, and strict recruitment of filial and upright graduates—the Xianfeng Emperor praised and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿出督師，援引內閣侍讀穆廕擢五品京堂，在軍機大臣上學習行走。

translations.literal: Saishanga went out to command troops and, relying on connections, promoted the Grand Secretariat reader Mu Yin to fifth-rank capital official to serve as learner-attache above the Grand Council ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Saishanga went out to command troops, he used his influence to promote Grand Secretariat reader Mu Yin to a fifth-rank capital post as learner-attache to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 廷魁疏劾其壞舊制，用私親，超擢太驟，易啟幸進之門，請俟賽尚阿還，令回章京本任，詔斥擅預黜陟，猶以素行端方，不之罪。

translations.literal: Tingkui memorialized impeaching this for breaking old regulations, employing private kin, promoting too suddenly, easily opening the gate of advancement by favor; he asked that after Saishanga returned, Mu be sent back to his original post as a Grand Council clerk; an edict rebuked him for presumptuously interfering in appointments and dismissals, yet because his conduct had been upright, he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Su Tingkui impeached this as a breach of precedent, nepotism, and reckless promotion that opened the door to favoritism; he asked that Mu Yin be returned to his clerk's post when Saishanga came back. An edict rebuked him for meddling in appointments, but because his conduct had been upright he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 上先隱其名，出疏示賽尚阿，賽尚阿退，飲台垣酒，問：「誰實彈我？

translations.literal: The Emperor first concealed his name and showed the memorial to Saishanga; when Saishanga withdrew he drank wine with the censorial officials and asked: "Who actually impeached me?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor first concealed his name and showed the memorial to Saishanga; when Saishanga withdrew he drank with the censorial officials and asked, "Who impeached me?"

sentences.zh: 」廷魁出席曰：「公負國，某不敢負公。

translations.literal: " Tingkui rose from his seat and said: "You have failed the state; I dare not fail you."
translations.idiomatic: " Su Tingkui rose and said, "You have failed the state; I dare not fail you."

sentences.zh: 」再以憂歸。

translations.literal: " He again returned home on bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: " He again returned home to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 四年，廣東紅巾匪起，將犯省城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Red Turban bandits rose in Guangdong and were about to attack the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Red Turban rebels rose in Guangdong and were about to attack the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 或獻議借外兵，以鋪捐為餉糈，力爭，罷其議。

translations.literal: Some proposed borrowing foreign troops, with shop levies as rations pay; he forcefully objected and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed borrowing foreign troops and funding them with shop levies; he forcefully objected and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 八年，英法聯軍踞廣州，廷魁與侍郎羅惇衍等倡設團防局，嚴清野，絕漢奸，招募東莞及三元里、佛山練勇得數万人，聲言戒期攻城，敵師出，擊斬百餘級。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Anglo-French allied army occupied Guangzhou; Tingkui together with Vice Minister Luo Dunyan and others initiated a local defense bureau, strictly cleared the countryside, cut off Chinese collaborators, recruited militia from Dongguan and Sanyuanli and Foshan numbering tens of thousands, announced a set date to storm the city; when the enemy forces came out they struck and killed more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Anglo-French allied army occupied Guangzhou; Su Tingkui, Vice Minister Luo Dunyan, and others founded a local defense bureau, enforced scorched-earth tactics, cut off collaborators, and recruited tens of thousands of militia from Dongguan, Sanyuanli, and Foshan; announcing a set date to storm the city, they ambushed the enemy when they came out and killed more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 敵始有戒心，稍戢，連艘北犯，既而天津議和，廣東敵兵未退，民益憤，廷魁等請留練局以防土寇。

translations.literal: The enemy then became wary and slightly restrained; linking ships they invaded northward; afterward peace was negotiated at Tianjin, yet enemy troops in Guangdong did not withdraw and popular anger grew; Tingkui and others asked to retain the militia bureau to guard against local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy grew wary and held back, then sailed north in force; after peace was negotiated at Tianjin the foreign troops in Guangdong did not withdraw and public anger mounted; Su Tingkui and others asked to keep the militia bureau to guard against local bandits.

sentences.zh: 敵謂既媾和何復募勇，且以懸金購領事巴夏禮為責言。

translations.literal: The enemy said that since peace had been made why recruit militia again, and also rebuked them on account of the posted reward for Consul Parkes.
translations.idiomatic: The foreigners protested that since peace had been made there was no need to recruit militia, and also rebuked them for posting a reward for the capture of Consul Harry Parkes.

sentences.zh: 議和大臣桂良慮撓成議，奏請撤局。

translations.literal: Peace negotiator Guiliang feared disruption of the settled agreement and memorialized requesting disbandment of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Peace negotiator Guiliang feared the agreement would be undermined and memorialized requesting that the bureau be disbanded.

sentences.zh: 初，艇匪擾廣寧，圍四會、肇慶，兵疲糧罄，或勸之去，廷魁曰：「予團防大臣也，誓與城為存亡！

translations.literal: Earlier, boat bandits harassed Guangning, besieged Sihui and Zhaoqing; troops were weary and grain exhausted; some urged him to leave; Tingkui said: "I am the local defense commissioner—I swear to live or die with the city!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, boat bandits harassed Guangning and besieged Sihui and Zhaoqing; troops were exhausted and supplies ran out; some urged him to flee. Su Tingkui said, "I am the local defense commissioner—I swear to live or die with this city!"

sentences.zh: 」會提督昆壽克梧州，以兵來援，城得完。

translations.literal: " It happened that Commander Kunshou captured Wuzhou and came with troops to relieve; the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: " Commander Kunshou captured Wuzhou and came with troops to relieve the siege; the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 疆臣屢欲上其功，皆固辭。

translations.literal: Frontier officials repeatedly wished to report his merit; he firmly declined all.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials repeatedly tried to report his merits; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 同治初，以中外大臣薦，授河南開歸陳許道，歷布政使，擢東河總督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, on recommendation of Chinese and foreign high officials, he was appointed circuit intendant of the Kai-Gui-Chen-Xu circuit in Henan, served as provincial treasurer, and was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, on recommendation of senior officials at home and abroad, he was appointed circuit intendant of the Kai-Gui-Chen-Xu circuit in Henan, served as provincial treasurer, and was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 七年，河決滎澤，未奪溜，革職留任，閱三月工竣，復之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Yellow River broke at Xingze without seizing the channel; he was stripped of office but retained in post; after three months the works were completed and he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Yellow River broke at Xingze without shifting its main channel; he was dismissed but kept in post; after three months the works were finished and he was restored.

sentences.zh: 逾年，內召，去官，稱疾歸。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned to the capital, left office, and returned home claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to the capital, left office, and returned home citing illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Guangxu reign.

sentences.zh: 朱琦，字伯韓，廣西臨桂人。

translations.literal: Zhu Qi, styled Bohán, was a native of Lingui in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qi, whose courtesy name was Bohán, came from Lingui in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父鳳森，嘉慶六年進士，官河南濬縣知縣，有政聲。

translations.literal: His father Fengsen passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Jiaqing, served as county magistrate of Jun County in Henan, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhu Fengsen earned his jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing, served as magistrate of Jun County in Henan, and was known for good governance.

sentences.zh: 滑縣教匪起，率團練御之，屢破賊，城守卒完。

translations.literal: When teaching-bandit rebels rose in Hua County he led militia to resist them, repeatedly defeated the bandits, and the city defense was ultimately preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When teaching-cult rebels rose in Hua County he led local militia against them, repeatedly defeated the rebels, and the city held.

sentences.zh: 遷河南府通判。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歿，祀名宦。

translations.literal: At his death he was enshrined among famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was enshrined among distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 琦，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Qi placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qi placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed revising editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he earned his jinshi, entered the Hanlin, and served as revising editor.

sentences.zh: 慕同里陳宏謀之為人，以氣節自勵。

translations.literal: He admired the character of his fellow townsman Chen Hongmou and took integrity as his own encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He admired the character of his fellow townsman Chen Hongmou and held himself to the same standard of integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，值海疆事定，禍機四伏，而上下復習委靡，言路多容默，深以為憂。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor; it happened that coastal affairs were settled, crises lurked on every side, yet above and below again fell into accustomed weakness, and the avenue of speech was largely silent—all of which he deeply worried over.
translations.idiomatic: He became a censor just as the coastal war ended; danger lurked on every side, yet court and country had relapsed into weakness and the avenue of remonstrance had fallen largely silent—all of which deeply troubled him.

sentences.zh: 著名實說，略曰：「天下有鄉曲之行，有大人之行。

translations.literal: He wrote a treatise On Reputation and Reality, which in summary says: "Under Heaven there is the conduct of the narrow village, and there is the conduct of the great man."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a treatise On Reputation and Reality, which in summary says: "Under Heaven there is the conduct of the narrow villager, and there is the conduct of the great man."

sentences.zh: 鄉曲、大人，其名也，考之其行，而察其有用與否，其實也。

translations.literal: "Village man" and "great man" are names; examining their conduct and observing whether they are useful or not—that is the reality.
translations.idiomatic: "Villager" and "great man" are only names; examining conduct and judging whether it serves the state—that is the reality.

sentences.zh: 世之稱者，曰謹厚，曰廉靜，日退讓，三者名之至美也，而不知此鄉曲之行也，非所謂大人者也。

translations.literal: What the age praises are called cautious and solid, called pure and quiet, called deferential—these three are names of utmost beauty, yet one does not know that this is the conduct of the village man, not what is called the great man.
translations.idiomatic: The age praises men as cautious and solid, pure and quiet, and deferential—these three are the finest names—yet this is the conduct of the villager, not of the great man.

sentences.zh: 大人之職，在於經國家、安社稷，有剛毅之大節，為人主畏憚；

translations.literal: The duty of the great man lies in ordering the state and securing the altars of soil and grain, having the great integrity of firm resolution, and making the ruler hold him in awe;
translations.idiomatic: The great man's duty is to govern the state and secure the realm; he must have the firm integrity that makes the ruler respect and fear him;

sentences.zh: 有深謀遠慮，為天下長計。

translations.literal: Having deep design and far-seeing concern, taking the long plan for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: and he must have deep design and far-seeing concern, planning for the long welfare of the empire.

sentences.zh: 合則留，不合以義去。

translations.literal: If in accord he stays; if not in accord he departs on grounds of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: If he agrees with the ruler he stays; if not, he departs on principle.

sentences.zh: 身之便安，不暇計也；

translations.literal: Personal ease and comfort he has no leisure to calculate;
translations.idiomatic: He has no time to calculate his own comfort;

sentences.zh: 世之指摘，不敢逃也。

translations.literal: The world's finger-pointing he does not dare flee.
translations.idiomatic: and he does not flee the world's blame.

sentences.zh: 今也不然。

translations.literal: Today it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is otherwise.

sentences.zh: 曰：吾為天下長計，則天下之釁必集於我；

translations.literal: One says: if I take the long plan for all under Heaven, then the world's quarrels will surely gather upon me;
translations.idiomatic: Men say: if I plan for the long welfare of the empire, every quarrel in the realm will fall on me;

sentences.zh: 吾為人主畏憚，則不能久於其位；

translations.literal: If I make the ruler hold me in awe, then I cannot long remain in my post;
translations.idiomatic: if I make the ruler respect and fear me, I cannot long keep my post;

sentences.zh: 不如謹厚、廉靜、退讓，此三者可以安坐而無患，而名又至美也。

translations.literal: Better cautious and solid, pure and quiet, deferential—these three allow one to sit at ease without trouble, and the reputation is also of utmost beauty.
translations.idiomatic: better to be cautious and solid, pure and quiet, and deferential—these three let one sit at ease without trouble, and the reputation is also most beautiful.

sentences.zh: 夫無患而可久於其位，又有天下美名，士何憚而不爭趨於此？

translations.literal: Now, without trouble and able to long remain in one's post, and also having a beautiful name under Heaven—what scholar would shrink from not all striving toward this?
translations.idiomatic: What scholar would not rush toward a path that keeps him safe in office, free from trouble, and crowned with the empire's finest reputation?

sentences.zh: 故近世所稱公卿之賢者，此三者為多矣。

translations.literal: Therefore among the high ministers praised in recent times, these three are the more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore among the high ministers praised in recent times, these three qualities predominate.

sentences.zh: 當其瓘冠襜裾，從容正步，趨於廊廟之間，上之人不疑，而非議不加，其沉深不可測也。

translations.literal: When they wear their caps and robes, walk calmly and properly, and hurry between corridor and temple, those above do not doubt them and censure is not added—their depth seems immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: When they wear their caps and robes, walk with calm dignity through the halls of state, and inspire no doubt above and no censure below, they seem immeasurably deep.

sentences.zh: 一旦遇大利害，搶攘無措，鉗口撟舌而莫敢言，而所謂謹厚、廉靜、退讓，至此舉無可用，於是始思向之為人主畏憚而有深謀遠慮者，不可得矣。

translations.literal: Once they meet great benefit or harm they are flustered and helpless, clamp their mouths and twist their tongues and none dare speak—and the so-called cautious and solid, pure and quiet, deferential, at this point are all useless; only then do they begin to think of those who once made the ruler hold them in awe and had deep design and far-seeing concern—they can no longer be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: But once a great crisis arrives they are flustered and helpless, clamp their mouths and twist their tongues, and dare not speak—and the vaunted caution, purity, and deference prove useless; only then do they realize that the men who once made the ruler respect them and planned for the long term are gone and cannot be found.

sentences.zh: 且謹厚、廉靜、退讓三者，非果無用也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three—cautious and solid, pure and quiet, deferential—are not truly useless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet caution, purity, and deference are not truly useless.

sentences.zh: 古有負蓋世之功而思持其後，挾震主之威而唯恐不終，未嘗不斤斤於此，故又於鎮薄俗、保晚節。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were those who bore world-shaking merit and thought to sustain their aftermath, who wielded awe-inspiring power over the ruler and yet feared not reaching the end—they never failed to be scrupulous in these, and so also in restraining shallow custom and preserving late integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity men who had achieved world-shaking merit and feared they could not sustain it, or who wielded power that awed the ruler and feared they would not finish well, were scrupulous in these virtues to restrain shallow custom and preserve their late integrity.

sentences.zh: 後世無其才而冒其位，安其樂而避其患，假於名之至美，僴然自以為足。

translations.literal: Later ages, without their talent yet usurping their posts, enjoying their ease while avoiding their peril, borrowing the most beautiful names, complacently deem themselves sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages, lacking such talent yet usurping such posts, enjoying the ease while avoiding the peril, borrow the finest names and complacently deem themselves sufficient.

sentences.zh: 是藏身之固，莫便此三者。

translations.literal: Thus for secure hiding there is nothing so convenient as these three.
translations.idiomatic: For secure self-preservation there is no better refuge than these three.

sentences.zh: 孔子之所謂鄙夫也，其究鄉愿也。

translations.literal: They are what Confucius called vulgar fellows; in the end they are village worthies.
translations.idiomatic: They are what Confucius called vulgar men; in the end they are mere village worthies.

sentences.zh: 是張禹、胡廣、趙戒之類也，甚矣其恥也！

translations.literal: They are of the kind of Zhang Yu, Hu Guang, and Zhao Jie—how great the shame!
translations.idiomatic: They are men of the sort of Zhang Yu, Hu Guang, and Zhao Jie—how shameful!

sentences.zh: 」於是數上疏切論時務，皆留中不報。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he repeatedly submitted memorials urgently discussing current affairs; all were retained at court and not answered.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted repeated memorials urgently discussing affairs of state; all were retained at court without response.

sentences.zh: 時咸推其抗直，稱為名御史。

translations.literal: At the time all praised his bold directness and called him a famous censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all praised his bold integrity and called him a famous censor.

sentences.zh: 琦以言既不見用，二十六年，告歸。

translations.literal: Because Qi's words were not employed, in the twenty-sixth year he asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When his counsel went unheeded, in the twenty-sixth year he asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 越數年，廣西群賊蜂起，其言皆驗。

translations.literal: After several years bandits swarmed up in Guangxi, and all his words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years bandits swarmed across Guangxi, and all his warnings proved true.

sentences.zh: 家居治團練，助守禦。

translations.literal: At home he managed militia training and assisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: At home he organized local militia and helped defend the region.

sentences.zh: 賊中梟傑張家祥者，悔罪投誠，當事猶疑之。

translations.literal: Among the bandits the chieftain Zhang Jiaxiang repented his crimes and submitted in good faith, yet those in charge still doubted him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain Zhang Jiaxiang repented and offered to surrender, but the authorities still doubted him.

sentences.zh: 琦知其忠勇可用，以全家保之，乃受降，改名國樑，卒為名將。

translations.literal: Qi knew his loyalty and courage could be used, pledged his whole family as guarantee, and then accepted the surrender; he was renamed Guoliang and in the end became a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qi saw that his loyalty and courage could be used, pledged his own family as guarantee, accepted his surrender, renamed him Guoliang, and he became a famous general.

sentences.zh: 琦以守城勞議敘，以道員候選。

translations.literal: On assessment of merit for defending the city, Qi was made a candidate for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in defending the city he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，再至京師。
