translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he again reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 居兩歲，從欽差大臣桂良至江蘇，無所遇，王有齡獨重之，有齡撫浙，闢贊軍事。

translations.literal: After two years he followed Imperial Commissioner Guiliang to Jiangsu, met with no success, but Wang Youling alone valued him; when Youling became governor of Zhejiang he was appointed to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he followed Imperial Commissioner Guiliang to Jiangsu without success, but Wang Youling alone valued him; when Wang became governor of Zhejiang he appointed Zhu to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪犯杭州，總理團練局。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Guangdong rebels attacked Hangzhou; he took charge of the militia bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Taiping rebels attacked Hangzhou, and he directed the militia bureau.

sentences.zh: 守清波門，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: He defended the Qingbo Gate; the city fell and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the Qingbo Gate; when the city fell he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 贈太常寺卿，予騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, given a hereditary post as Commandant of Cavalry, and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted a hereditary military rank, and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 琦學宗程、朱，詩古文皆有法，著有怡志堂集、台垣奏議。

translations.literal: Qi's learning followed the Cheng and Zhu schools; his poetry and ancient-style prose both had method; he authored the Yizhi Hall Collected Writings and Memorials from the Censorial Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qi's scholarship followed the Cheng-Zhu school; his poetry and prose were disciplined and accomplished. He wrote the Yizhi Hall Collected Writings and Memorials from the Censorial Terrace.

sentences.zh: 論曰：禁煙之議，創自黃爵滋，行之操切，而邊釁遂開，繼之游移而國威愈墮，誠不可以此歸咎始議之人。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The proposal to prohibit opium was initiated by Huang Juezi; carried out with harsh urgency, border hostilities thereupon opened; followed by vacillation and national prestige fell still further—truly one cannot on this account blame those who first proposed the measure.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Huang Juezi originated the proposal to ban opium; enforced with harsh urgency, it helped open the border war, and vacillation afterward only further degraded national prestige—yet one cannot blame those who first proposed the ban for what followed.

sentences.zh: 然謀國萬全，決胜千里，非恃意氣為也。

translations.literal: Yet planning the state with complete security and deciding victory a thousand li away do not rely on passionate spirit alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet securing the state and winning wars a thousand miles away cannot depend on passionate zeal alone.

sentences.zh: 行固維艱，言亦豈易易哉？

translations.literal: Action is indeed hard to sustain—how can speech be so easy?
translations.idiomatic: Action is hard enough—how much harder is it to speak wisely?

sentences.zh: 金應麟同被拔擢，亦始終主戰。

translations.literal: Jin Yinglin was likewise specially promoted and also consistently advocated war.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yinglin was likewise promoted and also consistently favored war.

sentences.zh: 陳慶鏞、蘇廷魁、朱琦時稱「三直」；

translations.literal: Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi were at the time called "the Three Upright";
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi were known at the time as "the Three Upright Ones";

sentences.zh: 合之應麟，又稱「四虎」。

translations.literal: adding Yinglin, they were also called "the Four Tigers."
translations.idiomatic: with Yinglin added, they were called "the Four Tigers."

sentences.zh: 所言有用有不用，凜凜然有生氣，要足以砭頑振懦矣。

translations.literal: What they said was sometimes used and sometimes not; stern and spirited, it was enough to pierce the stubborn and rouse the timid.
translations.idiomatic: Their counsel was sometimes heeded and sometimes ignored, yet it was stern and vital enough to pierce stubbornness and rouse the timid.
